The '''2026 Brent London Borough Council election''' took place on 7 May 2026, as part of the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections]]. All 57 seats on [[Brent London Borough Council]] were contested. The election took place alongside [[2026 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coughlan |first=Joe |date=2025-04-30 |title=London local elections, why they aren't in 2025 and when the next ones will be |url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/uk-world-news/london-local-elections-arent-any-31429137 |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=My London |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Local authority, combined authority, and county combined authority election cycles in England |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/election-timetable-in-england/election-timetable-in-england |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=GOV.UK |language=en}}</ref>

== Background ==
=== History ===
The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police and fire.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>

Since its formation, Brent has been variously under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control, [[no overall control]] and [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] control. Only Labour, Conservative, [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrat]] and [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green]] councillors have been elected to the council. The council has had an overall Labour majority since the [[2010 Brent London Borough Council election|2010 election]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grew |first=Tony |date=2026-04-02 |title=Brent: What to know ahead of the local elections 2026 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cy8lypvx7yxo |access-date=2026-04-12 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> The Liberal Democrats lost all but one of their seats in the [[2014 Brent London Borough Council election|2014 election]] and lost their final seat in the [[2018 Brent London Borough Council election|2018 election]], but returned to the council in the most recent election in [[2022 Brent London Borough Council election|2022]] winning three councillors. The incumbent leader of the council is Muhammed Butt, who has held that position since 2014.

=== Council term ===
Kathleen Fraser was suspended from the Labour group in June 2025 pending the outcome of an investigation.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Williams |first1=Grant |title=Labour tight-lipped as Brent deputy mayor suspended from group |url=https://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/news/25262544.brent-council-deputy-mayor-suspended-labour-group/ |access-date=29 December 2025 |work=Brent & Kilburn Times |date=24 June 2025 |language=en}}</ref> In October 2025, Labour councillor Rajan Seelan defected to the Conservatives.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/north-london-news/north-london-labour-councillor-defects-32782509|website=My London|last=Williams|first=Grant|date=31 October 2025|title=North London Labour councillor defects to Tories after 'demanding' ward from Lib Dems}}</ref> In December 2025, five Labour councillors defected to form the first Green grouping on the council.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-15 |title=Five Labour councillors defect as Polanski celebrates 'Green surge' |url=https://www.times-series.co.uk/news/25699647.five-brent-labour-councillors-defect-green-party/ |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=Times Series |language=en}}</ref> In March 2026, one Labour councillor defected to Your Party.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Francis |first=Martin |date=2026-03-27 |title=WEMBLEY MATTERS: Breaking: Labour loses another Brent councillor - this time to Your Party |url=https://wembleymatters.blogspot.com/2026/03/breaking-labour-loses-another-brent.html |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=WEMBLEY MATTERS}}</ref> Sunita Hirani was suspended from the Conservatives in April 2026.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Williams |first1=Grant |title=Councillor vows to 'clear her name' after suspension for 'alleged crime' |url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/north-london-news/brent-councillor-vows-clear-name-33774882 |access-date=5 May 2026 |work=My London |date=17 April 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

== Electoral process ==
Brent, as is the case all other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years, with the previous election having taken place in 2022. The election takes place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors will have as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over are entitled to vote in the election. People who live at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, are entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref> Voting in-person at polling stations takes place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters are able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election.<ref name=":1" />
